header:
Date: 2027-10-12
Start: 15:30 UTC
Duration: 49 minutes
Location: Zoom
Redwood attendees: Aiden Brooks, Maya Chen
AtlasPay attendees: Lena Ortiz, Marcus Vang, Priya Singh
summary: Weekly POC check-in focused on latency surges observed in AtlasPay staging: reviewed TTFT regressions, streaming handshake time, sequence-length dependent kernel choices, and a proposed Dedicated short-burst test. Agreed on profiling steps, Dedicated burst window, and follow-up artifacts to share.
topics: streaming handshake and early token pathing
microburst/hedging tradeoffs and Dedicated burst testing
transcript:
[00:00] Aiden: okay folks, thanks for joining, we are on for 45 minutes, quick agenda — microburst results, kernel decisions for 2k/4k, and next steps.
[00:14] Lena: yep, thanks, and hi — we saw another spike last night around 03:12 UTC where TTFT jumped to 430ms for a subset, so want to understand both root cause and mitigation.
[00:28] Maya: mm-hmm, can you share the sample traces? even a few requests that hit the spike helps us see if it's sequencing or KV cache thrash.
[00:37] Marcus: I'll grab them in a sec, just to flag — most of the traffic was streaming chat completions with long histories, we saw two distinct groups: short prompts and ~3k token histories.
[00:51] Priya: and from product side, the SLO we're targeting is 200ms median TTFT, 350ms 95th, anything above is noticeable to users.
[01:04] Aiden: good callout. from our side we ran a synthetic microburst yesterday but with a slightly different seqlen distribution — that's probably why the numbers didn't match.
[01:16] Lena: yeah, we suspected mismatch. Marcus, can you confirm typical seq lengths?
[01:21] Marcus: avg is ~1.1k but tail gets to 3.8k, and we haven't been trimming system prompts. also we have a few very chatty users.
[01:34] Maya: that tail explains kernel selection flips — our runtime will pick different kernels at thresholds leading to a jitter in latency. for 2k vs 4k we sometimes see an early token path that's faster but then stalls as kv cache warms.
[01:48] Priya: sorry, what's kv cache? I keep seeing K V cash in the docs — is that the same?
[01:53] Aiden: yeah, that's a common transcription thing — KV cache, key-value cache used for attention past tokens.
[02:02] Maya: right. in practice there are two things: handshake/streaming overhead (the streaming preamble adds ~20-40ms) and then kernel switches when the sequence crosses internal tiling thresholds.
[02:14] Marcus: we also saw an increase in cold start times when requests hit a different model variant, maybe the fallback to quantized model.
[02:23] Aiden: do you use multiple model variants in the pilot?
[02:26] Lena: yes, we have a smaller quantized variant in staging that we fall back to during heavy load. could that explain spikes?
[02:33] Maya: possibly — fallback means a different kernel set and sometimes a different init path. there's also prefix caching — if prefix cache misses occur it adds chattiness.
[02:45] Priya: ok so what's practical? we don't want to remove the fallback yet.
[02:50] Maya: practical steps: 1) we run a microburst profile that matches your production seqlen distribution (2k/4k tail) with streaming on; 2) we run the same workload on a short Dedicated pool so we can isolate kernel and network jitter; 3) we compare TTFT percentiles and kernel traces.
[03:08] Marcus: does the Dedicated pool change how KV cache behaves?
[03:11] Maya: not conceptually, but dedicated GPUs reduce noisy neighbor and scheduling variance, so if TTFT improves on Dedicated that points to multi-tenant scheduling or GPU eviction events.
[03:23] Aiden: and if it doesn't improve, then it's more about kernel decisions or sequence handling.
[03:30] Lena: about the microburst: can you document exact flags you'll use? we need to mirror prod as much as possible.
[03:36] Maya: yes, we'll use streaming enabled, continuous batching at a 16ms window, seqlen distribution CSV you'll provide, measurement of first token and first-byte, and kernel trace logging on the runtime side. we'll post a small runbook link after the call.
[03:52] Priya: linking to ops, are there security concerns with spinning up Dedicated for a short window? we need the one-pager for compliance.
[03:59] Aiden: absolutely — I'll attach the security/ops checklist and the KMS/HSM notes. also a note about audit logs and SSO access.
[04:10] Marcus: what about cost? we may need to justify the Dedicated 48h window and how pricing looks for burst blocks.
[04:16] Aiden: I'll send a burst-cost estimate and a canary rollback plan. rough numbers now: Dedicated short burst for 48h at the scale you asked is ~ $X (placeholder), exact to follow in the email.
[04:29] Lena: okay. walking through the timeline: we want the Dedicated test before the end of next week if possible.
[04:35] Maya: technically doable — we can run it as soon as you provision access, even same day once instances are up.
[04:42] Marcus: one more thing — our traces show occasional SSL renegotiation warnings, not sure if that's relevant.
[04:48] Aiden: could be infra unrelated but please include the snippets. sometimes network retries amplify TTFT.
[04:55] Priya: are there any model-level knobs we should try now without Dedicated? like reduced beam size or quant fallback thresholds?
[05:03] Maya: you can try reducing max_new_tokens and lower the history window as a mitigation, but that's product-level tradeoff. on the runtime side we can tune thresholding for kernel choice and reduce batch windows for high-priority routes.
[05:19] Lena: hmm batch windows - earlier you said 16ms. if we lower it, doesn't that increase cost?
[05:25] Maya: yes, smaller batch windows reduce latency but increase GPU utilization, so cost goes up. that's the familiar cost/latency trade.
[05:33] Marcus: do you have an automated suggestion tool for batching settings?
[05:36] Aiden: Redwood Optimize will produce suggestions, but for POC we'll provide a recommended config tuned to your seqlen distribution.
[05:43] Priya: and about competitors, we had a quick try of GoliathAI last month, they had lower median but worse 95th — so consistent with noisy infra.
[05:52] Maya: good to know. our focus is predictable SLOs under microburst.
[05:57] Lena: okay let's talk concrete deliverables. Marcus will collect traces and seqlen CSV, Maya will run the profile and upload results, Aiden will send pricing and security docs.
[06:09] Marcus: timeline: I'll have traces by EOD tomorrow.
[06:12] Maya: I'll schedule the profile run for day after trace upload.
[06:15] Aiden: and I'll send pricing/security by Wednesday.
[06:19] Priya: any concerns about function calling or tools hooks? some of our flows hit tool calls which add tail latency.
[06:26] Maya: yes tool calls are additive; we'll instrument them separately (we can tag tool calls in traces).
[06:31] Lena: another oddity — some of the spikes correlate with longer prompts that include PDF chunk embeddings, could embeddings be causing background IO?
[06:40] Marcus: we do a hybrid step where embeddings are looked up synchronously sometimes, that would add to TTFT.
[06:45] Maya: embedding syncs should be isolated; if they're blocking streaming, we need to async them or prefetch. we'll look for blocking calls in the trace.
[06:54] Aiden: wrap up — agreed items and we'll reconvene next Tuesday at the same time to review results.
[07:00] Priya: sounds good. thanks everyone.
[07:03] Lena: thanks.
[07:05] Aiden: thanks, bye.
